clue.text: Second offender to strike in error and evade duty

parts.note: crim is informal short for criminal, an offender
to shank a ball, in golf, is to mis-hit it off the club's heel

explanation.surface: A repeat offender lashes out by mistake while trying to dodge his obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRIMSHANK is British military slang for shirking work.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimshank is old British forces slang for shirking, dodging one's proper work.

clue.text: Get rid of old wine

definitions.meaning: to dismiss someone from a job, fire them
a dry white fortified wine imported from Spain in Shakespeare's day

explanation.definitionFit: Firing an employee is giving the sack; sack was also Falstaff's favourite sherry-like wine.

clue.text: Infantry soldier killing German, stunted figure

indicators.note: killing the German takes that letter out of the soldier word

parts.note: grunt is US slang for a foot soldier

explanation.surface: An infantryman kills a German, leaving a small, stunted body.
explanation.definitionFit: The runt of a litter is its smallest, undersized member, hence any stunted person.

clue.text: Badge seen in some castles built fringing river

indicators.note: fringing means the rearranged letters sit around the river letter
built means the letters of the words some castles are constructed into a new form

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An emblem is on display in castles constructed along a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' rearranges SOME CASTLES to MALTESE COSS, and 'fringing' puts it around R.
explanation.definitionFit: The eight-pointed cross of the Knights of Malta is worn as an insignia or badge of orders.

clue.text: It could be held by slowcoach as terrible

definitions.text: It could be held by slowcoach as terrible

indicators.note: held by means the letters are contained within the following run of words

explanation.surface: A dawdler would regard hurrying as an awful thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: speed is something a slowcoach would find terrible, and it sits inside 'slowcoacH AS TErrible'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurry or rush is exactly what a dawdler dreads, so the whole sentence points to rapid action.

clue.text: Obnoxious types blocking upcoming study? It doesn't matter

indicators.note: blocking means the pests sit inside, filling up the study word
upcoming, in a down clue, means the study word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study room
vermin are noxious creatures, figuratively obnoxious people

explanation.surface: Unpleasant people are getting in the way of the next research, but who cares?
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom brushes something aside as unimportant, just like saying 'forget it'.

clue.text: Noted tennis player with good service

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A famous tennis star is praised for a strong serve.
explanation.walkthrough: Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles; 'service' is the armed forces, not a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Steffi Graf is a German former world number one, a celebrated tennis champion.

clue.text: Piece about country lacking leader with breadth — resource in privation required?

indicators.note: about means the chess piece goes around the other letters

parts.note: a rook is a chess piece

indicators.note: lacking leader means the country word loses its first letter

parts.note: a nation is a country

explanation.surface: An article on a leaderless broad country asks what would be needed in hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain issued ration books during and after the Second World War, when food was scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: A wartime ration book held the coupons households needed to buy scarce food in times of shortage.

clue.text: Heartless guide in Ireland entering sensitive shipping area

indicators.note: entering means these letters go inside the word for sensitive

parts.note: fine as in finely tuned, delicate and sensitive

indicators.note: in means the cut guide word sits inside the Ireland abbreviation
Heartless means the middle letter of the guide word goes

parts.note: to steer is to guide

explanation.surface: A callous tour guide in Ireland moves into a delicate area of sea traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: Finisterre was a sea area of the BBC Shipping Forecast, renamed FitzRoy in 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: Finisterre was a named sea region in the British Shipping Forecast, off north-west Spain.

clue.text: Final prisoner left for all to see consumed by various vices

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: consumed by means these pieces are swallowed inside the shuffled letters
various suggests the letters of vices take varied forms

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A convict in his last stage is plainly eaten up by assorted bad habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Decisive evidence or a deciding result is final, settling the matter beyond doubt.

clue.text: Shock curtailed showy performance

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, the last letter cut

parts.note: a stunt is a showy feat done to draw attention

explanation.surface: A flashy act was cut short by a sudden scare.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock someone is to daze or stagger them, leaving them dumbfounded.

clue.text: Read source of entertainment among the lads after excitement — this?

definitions.text: Read source of entertainment among the lads after excitement — this?

parts.note: to scan is to read through

indicators.note: among means the first letter sits within the lads
after excitement means the letters of the lads have been stirred up
source of means only the opening letter of entertainment is used

explanation.surface: Asks what the lads, excited, would read for amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' gives E, 'among' puts it in THE LADS, and 'after excitement' shuffles that to DALSHEET after SCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip tabloid full of lurid stories is the reading matter the excited lads would enjoy.

clue.text: Superficially attractive deception largely after pool with promises of payment

indicators.note: after means the cut deception word follows the pool word

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a trick is a deception
IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: A con trick follows a betting pool backed only by IOUs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meretricious is showy and alluring on the surface but of no real worth.

clue.text: I miss place arranged for devotion to a study?

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of I miss place are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone misses where things were placed in a study.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialism is a field one concentrates on exclusively, a dedicated area of expertise.

clue.text: Special note about wave with excellent waxy substance

indicators.note: about means the first pieces wrap around the rest

parts.note: ti is a note of the sol-fa scale
a perm is a hair wave
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A special note concerns a top-notch wave and a waxy product.
explanation.definitionFit: Spermaceti is a white wax from the sperm whale's head, once used for candles and ointments.

clue.text: Something in pot on island is spicy stuff

parts.note: pepper is what a pepper pot holds
taken as written

explanation.surface: An item in the cooking pot on a holiday island turns out to be hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy, peppery Italian-style dried sausage.

clue.text: Old hotel accommodating writer above river showing hospitality to all?

indicators.note: above, in a down clue, means the first part comes before the river
accommodating means the old hotel letters take in the writer

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a pen is a writing instrument
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: An aging riverside hotel puts up an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping open house means welcoming any visitors freely, offering hospitality to everyone.

clue.text: Illustrious snob lengthily detained

indicators.note: detained means the letters are held inside the words snob lengthily

explanation.surface: A famous snob was kept in custody for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble describes someone distinguished and eminent, of high rank or character.

clue.text: Nurse, perhaps, about to enter estate?

indicators.note: to enter means the short word goes inside the vehicle word

parts.note: an estate car is a station wagon
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A nurse might be on her way into a country property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'estate' suggests land, but it is an estate car, the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse is one example of someone who looks after the sick, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Attempt to shift over a dune

indicators.note: shift means the letters of over a dune are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone tries to move across a sand hill.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to try hard; as a noun it is a serious effort or try.

clue.text: One specialising in numbers?

parts.note: numbers here are things that numb, not figures

explanation.surface: Asks for an expert with figures.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a mathematician or accountant, but 'numbers' means numbing agents.
explanation.definitionFit: This doctor administers drugs that numb patients before surgery.

clue.text: Time of change almost involving party in house

indicators.note: involving means the cut change word wraps around the party word
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a turn is a time of change, as in the turn of the year
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A period of transition nearly involves a political party in the House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' means a royal dynasty, not a building or parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were a royal dynasty of England, a ruling house from 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: Brace is cut reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, a homophone

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: A support is said to have been trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace of pheasants is two of them, a couple.

clue.text: Woman's beach primarily in bay perhaps

parts.note: her is the female possessive

indicators.note: primarily means just the opening letter of beach

explanation.surface: A woman's beach is chiefly in a bay, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' suggests the coast, but it is the bay laurel used in cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay leaves are an example of a culinary plant, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Regulars in wild began plan

indicators.note: regulars means every other letter of the words wild began

explanation.surface: Regular attendees at a raucous party began a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can be a scheme or intention, a plan for action.

clue.text: Peer around northern river and start to chomp a rich food

indicators.note: around means the peer wraps the other pieces

parts.note: a duke is a peer of the realm
the Dee is a river in Scotland, Wales and England

indicators.note: start to means just the first letter of chomp

explanation.surface: A nobleman by a northern river begins to munch on something luxurious.
explanation.walkthrough: Dundee cake is a Scottish fruit cake topped with almonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Dundee cake is a dense, rich fruit cake decorated with whole almonds.

clue.text: One in service is appointed by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means a word heard alike

parts.note: made, as in made chairman, means appointed

explanation.surface: A servant is chosen, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is a female domestic servant, someone in service.

clue.text: Hat brother lost, one noted for attracting attention

indicators.note: lost means the letters of hat brother are in disarray

explanation.surface: A sibling who mislaid his hat is now a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartthrob is a famous, attractive man adored by fans.
